description: Phase 8: Tokenized MMF / overnight liquidity parking (JLTXX-inspired, PRD.md §24). Institutions park idle settlement-treasury balances in a simulated tokenized money-market fund (mockJLT), accrue daily yield, and recall T+0 when a payment needs the liquidity. Guardrails: institutional-only eligibility, explicit per-entity opt-in, park/recall events on the hash-chained audit log, strict segregation from payment escrow. Testnet-only, fully simulated yield, no real securities.

userStories.title: TokenizedMMF Solidity contract
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a permissioned tokenized-MMF contract so idle stablecoin can be parked into share tokens and redeemed, with operator-controlled daily index accrual.
acceptanceCriteria: New contracts/TokenizedMMF.sol (Solidity 0.8.24): holds one approved ERC-20 asset, operator-only subscribe(address onBehalfOf, uint256 assetAmount) pulls the asset and mints shares at the current index, operator-only redeem(address onBehalfOf, uint256 shares) burns shares and returns the asset at the current index
Operator-only accrue(uint256 newIndex) with require(newIndex >= currentIndex) — index is monotonic, starts at 1e18
Events emitted: Subscribed(account, assetAmount, shares), Redeemed(account, shares, assetAmount), Accrued(oldIndex, newIndex)
Non-operator calls to subscribe/redeem/accrue revert
Funds held by TokenizedMMF are never routed through or held by PaymentSettlement (separate contract, no cross-calls)
npm run compile succeeds
Contract behavior tests added under tests/integration/ (subscribe/redeem round-trip at index 1e18, redeem after accrual returns more asset, operator restriction reverts)
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Park: sweep idle treasury balance into the MMF
userStories.description: As a treasury manager, I want to park idle treasury stablecoin into the tokenized MMF so it earns simulated overnight yield.
acceptanceCriteria: New lib/treasury.ts with park({ networkId, asset, amount }): converts the decimal-string amount via toBaseUnits (bigint end to end, no JS floats), approves and calls subscribe via operatorWrite, creates an ACTIVE TreasuryPosition with the park tx hash
Park refuses (throws a typed error) when the amount exceeds unreserved treasury balance — reserved liquidity for pending payments can never be parked
Park writes an audit event (audit(...) from lib/audit.ts) with type TREASURY_PARKED including network, asset, amount, and tx hash
DB test: parking reduces available treasury liquidity reported by the existing liquidity logic and creates the position row
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Recall: T+0 redemption back to the settlement asset
userStories.description: As a treasury manager, I want to recall a parked position instantly so liquidity is available when a payment needs it.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/treasury.ts gains recall(positionId): redeems the position's shares at the current index via operatorWrite, marks the position RECALLED with recalledAt and the recall tx hash
Redeemed asset (principal plus any accrued yield) returns to the treasury wallet and is reflected in available liquidity
Recall writes an audit event TREASURY_RECALLED with position id, shares, asset amount returned, and tx hash
Recalling a non-ACTIVE position throws; the position row is never deleted (append-only history)
Integration test: park then recall round-trips the principal at unchanged index
Tests pass
Typecheck passes

userStories.title: Simulated daily yield accrual
userStories.description: As a treasury manager, I want parked balances to accrue realistic daily yield so the demo shows the value of overnight parking.
acceptanceCriteria: lib/treasury.ts gains accrueDaily(networkId): computes one day of yield at a configurable annual rate (constant, default 3.5% APY) using integer/bigint index math and calls accrue(newIndex) on the contract
Position current value is derived (shares x currentIndex), never stored mutably on the position row
Accrual writes an audit event TREASURY_ACCRUED with old index, new index, and rate
Unit test: known index and rate produce the expected new index (deterministic, no wall-clock dependence)
Integration test: park, accrue once, recall returns more than parked principal
